Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: 'anvil song' — the rhythmic ringing of hammer on anvil that traditionally signaled an active forge to the village. Counter to Patternweld (technical to the point of opacity) and Forge Index (loses the craft register). Anvilsong is a single-word compound that lives on signage and a stamp.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern blacksmithing has expanded from architectural ironwork into knife-making, sculpture, and small-run hardware. The opening is for a brand that names the rhythm of the forge plainly.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Bigfoot Forge (bigfootironworks.com) plays the modern-architectural peer. Tools for Working Wood (toolsforworkingwood.com) holds the heritage-trade reference. Brent Bailey Forge (brentbaileyforge.com) is the knife-and-tool middle. We sit as a rhythm-named modern smithing brand.
Modern.positioningStatement: Anvilsong is a modern blacksmithing workshop named for the rhythmic ringing of hammer on anvil.

targetAudience.primary: Design-aware homeowners and small architects 30-55 commissioning hand-forged hardware, knives, and small-run ironwork.
behaviors: Commission a single piece by email
Care about hammer marks staying visible
Return for a second commission within two years

dos: Name the smith on every piece
donts: Romanticize the forge with soft focus

Modern.logoDirection: Wordmark: ANVILSONG set in a confident grotesk, one word, slightly extended. Small mark: a single anvil silhouette with three short rule-lines above it — the ringing — used as the maker's stamp on the metal.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for commission specs
typography.rationale: One grotesk family plus its mono — the commission-sheet register.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Damascus steel — the historic pattern-welded steel tradition associated with the city of Damascus, used today as a generic technique name across knife-making and decorative ironwork. Damascus is a geographic place name, not a registered brand in this trade. Counter to Journeyman & Crown (looser) and The Worshipful Forge (treads close to a livery-company name).
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury blacksmithing is a small commission-only category — pattern-welded blades, gates, fireplace tools, and architectural ironwork for collectors and listed buildings. The buyer is a collector, an estate manager, or an architect.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Bob Kramer Knives (kramerknives.com) plays the high-end pattern-welded peer. Britannia Forge (britanniaforge.co.uk) holds the heritage-architectural reference. James Price Blacksmith (jamespriceblacksmith.co.uk) is the listed-buildings middle. We sit as a commission-only pattern-welded house.
Luxury.positioningStatement: House of Damascus is a commission-only blacksmithing house specializing in pattern-welded steel blades and architectural ironwork.

targetAudience.primary: Collectors, estate managers, and architects commissioning pattern-welded pieces with a documented process.
behaviors: Wait twelve to twenty-four months for delivery
Care about the pattern, the layers, and the smith's mark

dos: Document the pattern and the layer count
Name the smith and the commission number
Send a paper certificate with each piece
donts: Photograph the smith in lifestyle settings

Luxury.logoDirection: Wordmark: HOUSE OF DAMASCUS set in a refined serif, three lines centered. A hallmark — a single small Damascus-pattern swatch — used on the certificate and the maker's mark on the metal.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and certificates
typography.secondary: Garamond Premier Pro for body and commission letters
typography.rationale: Two classical English serifs — the commission-house register.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the anvil — the single object that defines the trade. Counter to Hammer. (over-punctuated) and Quench (too process-specific). Anvil is the trade noun, single syllable, the object on the floor.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal blacksmithing brands serve the design-literate buyer commissioning a single hand-forged piece. The opening is for a single-word trade-noun brand with no narrative theater.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Brent Bailey Forge (brentbaileyforge.com) plays the considered-minimal peer. Smith & Forge (limited reference) holds a similar register. Pieh Tool Company (piehtoolco.com) is the heritage-supply middle. We sit as the single-word minimal option.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Anvil is a minimal blacksmithing workshop — one smith, one anvil, one rate card.

targetAudience.primary: Homeowners and small architects 30-50 commissioning a single hand-forged piece.

dos: Publish the rate card on the home page
Show the piece, not the forge
Confirm the commission in one line

Minimal.logoDirection: Wordmark: ANVIL set very large in a clean modern sans, five letters, one word. No symbol.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for the rate card
typography.rationale: Clean Diatype with its mono — the single-trade register.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Anchor: 'the village smithy' — the long-standing trade phrase made canonical by Longfellow's 1840 poem, used today across heritage-trade firms. Counter to Henry & Hale Ironworks (paired surname risks reading as a real firm) and Blackiron Holdings (generic). Village Smithy Co. is a phrase, not a surname, with a corporate suffix.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate blacksmithing operates across architectural ironwork, heritage restoration, and large-scale hand-forged hardware. The buyer is an architect, an estates manager, or a heritage-restoration project lead.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Britannia Forge (britanniaforge.co.uk) plays the heritage-architectural peer. Cambridge Architectural Mesh (cambridgearchitectural.com) holds the broader architectural-metal reference. Topp Steel (toppsteel.com) is the institutional-fabrication middle. We sit as a multi-site architectural smithing firm.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Village Smithy Co. is a multi-site architectural blacksmithing firm specializing in heritage restoration and hand-forged hardware programs.

targetAudience.primary: Architects, estates managers, and heritage-restoration project leads commissioning hand-forged ironwork at scale.

dos: Lead with restoration credentials and project list
Speak to architects and estates managers
donts: Photograph individual smiths as the hero shot

Corporate.logoDirection: Wordmark: VILLAGE SMITHY CO. set in an institutional serif, three lines centered. A small mark — a single anvil-and-hammer silhouette — used on the contract cover.

typography.rationale: A reading serif plus a clean grotesk — the heritage-trade firm register.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the bellows (the forge's air supply) and the bone (a traditional knife-handle material). Counter to The Sparking Anvil (more illustrative than ownable) and John Henry's Hammer (borrows a folk-song proper noun). Bellows & Bone is the alliterative trade pairing that lives on a label.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative blacksmithing brands lean on knife-making, small-batch hardware, and a strong maker's voice. The opening is for an alliterative paired-noun brand that names the forge's air and the knife's handle plainly.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Brent Bailey Forge (brentbaileyforge.com) plays the maker-led peer. Cut Brooklyn (cutbrooklyn.com) holds the knife-maker middle. Smith Shop (smithshopdetroit.com) is the workshop-school reference. We sit as a paired-noun creative smithing brand.
Creative.positioningStatement: Bellows & Bone is a creative blacksmithing and knife-making workshop named for the forge's air and the knife's handle.

targetAudience.primary: Home cooks and design-aware buyers 28-50 commissioning a single knife or small-run hardware.
behaviors: Photograph the maker's mark on the blade

dos: Name the smith and the handle material on every piece
Write the order confirmation in the smith's voice
Use the bellows-and-bone pairing as the visual hook
donts: Photograph the workshop in soft focus

Creative.logoDirection: Wordmark: BELLOWS & BONE set in a warm display serif with a hand-drawn ampersand. Small mark: a small bellows over a single bone-handle silhouette — used as the maker's stamp.

typography.rationale: A warm display serif plus a clean grotesk — the maker-led register.
